scene: Full vertical ascent, especially the three waterfall shafts
title: Connect every waterfall to a visible source and receiver

position.description: Waterfalls at approximately (7,24), (29,10), and (39,8); only the far-right shaft aligns with the pool at x38–41

steps: Open level-map.html?w=4.
Set Gems to 5/5.
Turn off Beats and Route and choose Fit.
Trace each waterfall from its upper edge to its lower edge.
trigger: Inspect the complete waterfall network in the flattened rendered world.
observation: All three pale shafts begin in open air without a visible lip, channel, cloud, or spring. The left and centre shafts meet dry base terrain, while the only pool is beneath the far-right shaft.
player_interpretation: The water reads as three mechanically inserted vertical ribbons rather than one mountain water system.
intended_logic: Recipe comments describe waterfalls giving life to the climb and pouring past ledges into the pool.
inferred_cause: The recipe supplies waterfall top rows independently of visible source and receiver geometry. This is an authoring inference, not a confirmed renderer defect.
recommendation: Compose each retained fall with an explicit source lip or upper basin and a visible receiver such as the existing pool, a new contained basin, mist, or a channel. Remove any shaft that cannot be made part of the same readable system.
acceptance_criteria: At both target phone viewports, every visible waterfall can be traced to an implied source before its upper edge leaves frame.
Every shaft visibly terminates in water, mist, or a contained channel rather than dry ground.
The three elements read as one intentional mountain water system during the climb.
recurring_cause: Repeated waterfall authoring pattern shared with W07-F01; likely recipe placement, with a possible shared validation gap.

validation: Fresh-origin flattened-map comparison passed for W04-F01.
limitations: Native phone traversal and camera framing were not retested; those remain a separate deferred audit.

world_name: Al-Lail — the night and the two ways
scene: Long night ascent from the valley floor through the forked middle face
title: Make the night-climb waterfalls belong to one water system

position.description: Waterfalls at approximately (9,40), (33,58), and (44,26); the only pool sits at x43–47 on the valley floor

steps: Open level-map.html?w=7.
Set Gems to 21/21.
Turn off Beats and Route and choose Fit.
Trace all three waterfall shafts through the full-height climb.
trigger: Inspect the complete waterfall network in the flattened rendered world.
observation: The three shafts start below unrelated open air. The left and centre falls terminate on dry valley terrain; only the far-right fall reaches the small pool.
player_interpretation: The repeated vertical strips feel decorative and arbitrary, weakening the otherwise coherent bottom-to-summit night story.
intended_logic: Recipe comments say the falls pour past the mountain faces into the pool.
inferred_cause: Waterfalls are authored as independent vertical spans without paired source and receiver set pieces. This is inferred from the recipe and rendered map.
recommendation: Route the visible falls through ledge-edge sources toward the valley pool, or convert the two dry-ending shafts into mist-fed magical falls with explicit visual emitters and dissipating ends.
acceptance_criteria: Each waterfall has a visible or strongly implied emitter at its top.
The left and centre shafts no longer stop on dry ground without mist, basin, or channel treatment.
The pool and falls read as a connected system from both the lower valley and the upper switchbacks.
recurring_cause: Same recipe-authoring pattern as W04-F01; consider a shared authoring check after the two world fixes are composed.

validation: Fresh-origin flattened-map comparison passed for W07-F01.
limitations: Native phone traversal and camera framing were not retested; those remain a separate deferred audit.

scene: Central Wise Tree and pillar-of-light landmark at x≈42.5
title: Give the One Light a legible silhouette at full restoration

position.description: World centre, pillar of light behind the Wise Tree

steps: Open level-map.html?w=9.
Set Gems to 4/4.
Turn off Beats and Route and choose Fit.
Compare the central light column with the surrounding sky and hills.
trigger: View the intended landmark at maximum restoration.
observation: Even at 4/4 gems, the vertical light veil is only slightly warmer than the sky and hill layers. The Wise Tree is more legible than the world-defining light behind it.
player_interpretation: The centre reads as another quiet tree cluster rather than the singular monument promised by the world's composition.
intended_logic: The recipe describes a radiant monument visible from everywhere and widening rings that enclose the world.
inferred_cause: Landmark alpha and hue are too close to the restored palette at the flattened-map scale; gameplay visibility remains to be spot-checked.
recommendation: Strengthen the landmark's edge, ground contact, or localized contrast while preserving its soft, non-figurative character. Prefer a recognizable base and vertical core over simply increasing overall brightness.
acceptance_criteria: At 0/4 and 4/4 gems, the child can identify the same central landmark before reaching it.
At both phone viewports, the pillar remains distinguishable from sky and hills without obscuring the Wise Tree or gems.
The monument still reads as light rather than a solid platform or wall.
recurring_cause: World-specific contrast issue within a broader set of faint custom landmarks.

validation: Fresh-origin flattened-map comparison passed for W09-F01.
limitations: Native phone traversal and camera framing were not retested; those remain a separate deferred audit.

scene: Elephant-rock landmark over the far third of the route
title: Anchor the elephant rock to the distant horizon

position.description: Background landmark centred near tile x70, rows 5.75–7.5

steps: Open level-map.html?w=13.
Set Gems to 5/5.
Turn off Beats and Route and choose Fit.
Inspect the grey elephant-shaped form above the far hills.
trigger: View the landmark in the complete flattened world.
observation: The compact grey silhouette sits in open sky with no visible foothill, haze bridge, or base connection. Its underside is clean enough to resemble a floating stone capsule.
player_interpretation: The form may read as an unexplained floating object before it reads as a distant elephant-shaped rock.
intended_logic: The recipe intends a small, hazed, distant rock that belongs to the far hill layer and cannot be mistaken for a platform.
inferred_cause: The landmark base is placed above the visible hill silhouette and the mist wash is too subtle to connect the layers.
recommendation: Seat the lower contour into a far-hill shoulder or extend a stronger mist/terrain bridge beneath it. Preserve the small scale, gentle elephant suggestion, and background-only status.
acceptance_criteria: The silhouette visibly belongs to the far horizon at both phone viewports.
Its base no longer presents a clean floating underside.
It remains clearly non-collidable and subordinate to the route and ordered gems.
recurring_cause: Related to W17-F01 and W20-F01: custom background landmarks lack sufficient horizon integration.

validation: Fresh-origin flattened-map comparison passed for W13-F01.
limitations: Native phone traversal and camera framing were not retested; those remain a separate deferred audit.

scene: Painted reflected road spanning tiles x5–83 behind the playable route
title: Separate the reflected road from solid bridge language

position.description: Background band across world rows approximately 8.5–10.5

steps: Open level-map.html?w=18.
Set Gems to 6/6.
Turn off Beats and Route and choose Fit.
Compare the long reflected band with the playable terrace silhouettes below it.
trigger: View the full reflected-road set piece without map overlays.
observation: The reflection is bounded by long, straight, parallel edges and contains a continuous horizontal line. At world scale it resembles a suspended glass bridge or elevated route more than water.
player_interpretation: A child may treat the upper band as a second traversable path or destination instead of an unreachable reflection.
intended_logic: The recipe intends a rippling, upside-down, non-collidable reflection across still water behind the one true road.
inferred_cause: The band geometry is too rectilinear and uniform relative to the organic hills and terrace language; live confusion has not been observed directly.
recommendation: Break the bridge-like silhouette with stronger water cues: irregular shore edges, more visible ripples, softer end fades, and clearer inverted reflections. Preserve the single-path metaphor and non-collidable implementation.
acceptance_criteria: At both phone viewports, the upper band is immediately readable as water/reflection rather than a platform.
The playable road remains the only high-contrast continuous route line.
The reflected elements remain visibly inverted and do not compete with ordered gems.
recurring_cause: World-specific composition problem; do not group with horizon-grounding fixes despite also being background paint.

validation: Fresh-origin flattened-map comparison passed for W18-F01.
limitations: Native phone traversal and camera framing were not retested; those remain a separate deferred audit.

scene: Safe-city landmark above the early-middle route
title: Make the safe city perceptible without making it solid

position.description: Background landmark centred near tile x31.5, around row 7.9

steps: Open level-map.html?w=20.
Set Gems to 8/8.
Turn off Beats and Route and choose Fit.
Inspect the expected city region over the third beat.
trigger: View the landmark at maximum restoration, when its windows should be fully kindled.
observation: The city silhouette and kindled windows are effectively lost against the restored sky and overlapping hill tones; the expected area reads as ordinary horizon.
player_interpretation: The safe-city beat has no memorable skyline marker, so the route's promised orchard-to-city-to-mount progression is visually compressed.
intended_logic: The recipe describes a small, distant walled city whose windows kindle with collection and whose position marks ayah 3.
inferred_cause: The landmark's haze alpha and palette mixing leave too little contrast at full restoration; live close-range visibility is unverified.
recommendation: Increase silhouette separation or window clustering and seat the city into a distinct far-hill shoulder. Keep it small, hazed, background-only, and clearly non-collidable.
acceptance_criteria: At 0/8 and 8/8 gems, the same city silhouette is perceptible from the ayah-3 approach at both phone viewports.
The city remains subordinate to ordered gems and cannot be mistaken for playable terrain.
The orchard, city, hollow, and summit read as four distinct route chapters.
recurring_cause: Related to W13-F01 and W17-F01: custom background landmarks do not integrate strongly enough with the shared horizon.

validation: Fresh-origin flattened-map comparison passed for W20-F01.
limitations: Native phone traversal and camera framing were not retested; those remain a separate deferred audit.
